summary: `Chain.pendingDir` replaces `Chain.pendingPath`: the ledger is a directory of `<tag>.json`, its own `*.json` is the listing, and a ship `git rm`s exactly what shipped

per.section: The ledger is a directory — one entry per file

acceptance: Every queue read and the ship resolve `Chain.pendingDir`; a `*.json` directly under it is an entry and a subdirectory is not walked; a file whose `tag` disagrees with its filename is refused naming both; an absent or empty directory reads as nothing pending; `flume status` and `flume check` read the directory.
tests: a *.json directly under the pending directory is an entry and a subdirectory is not walked
an entry file whose tag disagrees with its filename is refused naming both
a parse failure names the entry file it read
an absent pending directory reads as nothing pending
a ship removes exactly the shipped entries' files and edits no other entry
flume status reports pending: unparsable when one entry file is malformed
notes: Tag uniqueness becomes the filesystem's, so the composed list schema's duplicate issue goes; the `pendingGate` drift blockquote is already retired. This repo's own live queue is an operator cutover — `.flume/` is outside every phase's fence — and the legacy file rides planArtifacts so a plan tick can `git rm` it, the allowance LEGACY_QUESTIONS_REL already takes.

summary: A build tick stakes `<git-common-dir>/flume/claims/<slug>` before provisioning and drops it when the attempt ends; selection skips a claimed entry

per.section: Claims — an entry in flight is left alone

acceptance: A claim exists from before its entry's worktree is provisioned until the attempt ends, with the ship or the teardown; `TickContext.claimed` and `TickResult.claimedTags` report the set the tick read; selection skips a claimed entry and a claim held by a dead pid is reclaimed.
tests: a build tick stakes its entry's claim before provisioning the worktree
the claim is removed when an attempt ends without shipping
selection skips an entry another tick holds a claim on
TickResult.claimedTags reports the claims the tick read
a claim held by a dead pid is reclaimed by the next selection
notes: Reported, never inferred: nothing outside the engine re-reads the claims directory. What a producer does about a claimed entry it would have changed stays the chain's.

edit.description: the third check, and `opts.hint` over all three
wire it afterMerge on the producer phases

summary: pendingGate's third check: a gated commit leaves a claimed entry's file byte-identical, or is refused naming the entry and its holder

per.section: `pendingGate` — validation and fence pre-check as an opt-in builtin

acceptance: A commit that edits or removes a claimed entry's file fails pendingGate naming the entry and the holding pid; an edit to an unclaimed entry passes; the check runs afterMerge over the merged tree and `opts.hint` appends to its message as to the other two.
tests: pendingGate refuses a commit that edits a claimed entry's file, naming the entry and the holder
pendingGate refuses a commit that removes a claimed entry's file
pendingGate passes a commit that edits an unclaimed entry
opts.hint appends to the claim-check violation message
notes: afterMerge because a pre-merge read passes over exactly the tree the collision is not in; uncontended under one producer. It is the section's only merged-tree gate: there is no duplicate refusal beside it — the drain folds a duplicate instead (THE-DRAIN-FOLDS-A-DUPLICATE-FINDING).
